correctness.rationale: For every erasure level t, the necessary and sufficient detector-witness inequalities are derived. Six antipodal pairs and 15 unions of two pairs reduce all adjacent separators to occupancy inequalities. This proves t1 lower bound 5, t2 lower bound 6, t3 lower bound 11, and t4 only all vertices. Exact 120 t1 and 20 t2 counts follow by five-coordinate Hamming projection and cyclic C5 neighborhood-pattern inequalities; the t3/t4 constructions and t>=5 impossibility follow from four-vertex differences. The twenty face-indexed induced 3-suns and parity-based unique completion are explicitly derived. Independently executed full 4096-subset Python set and C++ bitmask verifiers, constructed from different literal graph representations, affirm every census, all twenty suns, all 120 completions and 15 antipodal separator blocks. Proof and full reproducible code included.

value.rationale: The number of detectors necessary to preserve vertex identification after up to zero, one, two or three erasures is an intrinsic and motivated fault-tolerance invariant on a canonical highly symmetric graph. The sharp discontinuity from six to eleven sensors, exact face/3-sun classification of twenty resilient optima and unique minimum-size completion of all 120 ordinary optima give structural information relevant to graph identification and placement, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a restatement of a database count. The result is a natural complete fixed-graph classification; no speculative broader theorem is asserted.
